recent_posts.title: Remaking three mobile games in Unity in one hour each
recent_posts.summary: A developer attempts to recreate three popular (and absurd) mobile games — Last War, Butt Clash, and Eating Simulator — in Unity within one hour each. The video covers rapid prototyping techniques including basic movement scripts, bullet spawning, soft body physics simulation using circles and springs, and 3D asset integration. Each game is built from scratch with free assets, minimal polish, and comedic commentary, then compared side-by-side with the originals. The soft body physics segment offers a brief but genuine explanation of how rigid body circles connected by springs can simulate squishy objects.

recent_posts.title: A.I. Learns To Play HAPPY WHEELS
recent_posts.summary: A developer recreates Happy Wheels from scratch in Unity and trains an AI using genetic algorithms to play the game. The project involves building physics-based bike mechanics, ragdoll characters, gore effects, and level design. The AI learns through evolution simulation, where populations of players perform random movements, the best performers are selected to create mutated offspring, and the process repeats until successful completion. The final AI discovers creative solutions like launching dismembered character parts toward the finish line at high speed.

recent_posts.title: Hiring five Fiverr developers to build RPG games with $1000 budgets
recent_posts.summary: A content creator hired five Fiverr developers with a $1000 budget each to create RPG games based on the same prompt requesting a Skyrim-like experience. The video showcases gameplay from all five submissions, featuring diverse approaches including souls-like combat, pixel art adventures, and atmospheric 3D environments. Each game demonstrated unique mechanics, art styles, and creative interpretations of the brief, with varying levels of polish and gameplay depth.

recent_posts.title: Creating the same game in 10 minutes vs 1 hour vs 10 hours
recent_posts.summary: A developer challenges himself to create the same naval combat game in three different time constraints: 10 minutes, 1 hour, and 10 hours using Unity. The progression shows how additional development time allows for better water physics, improved graphics, multiplayer functionality, and more polished gameplay mechanics. Each version is tested with a friend in multiplayer mode, revealing both the potential and limitations of rapid game development.

recent_posts.title: Building a desktop Snake game that deletes Windows system files
recent_posts.summary: A developer creates a dangerous version of the classic Snake game that runs on the Windows desktop, where eating 'apples' (system files) actually deletes critical System32 files from the computer. The project involves automating desktop interactions, implementing Snake game mechanics using file icons as game pieces, and ultimately destroying a computer by deleting essential Windows system files including Explorer.exe and Task Manager.

recent_posts.title: AI tackles Minesweeper for leaderboard glory
recent_posts.summary: The post explores using AI to achieve top scores in Minesweeper by analyzing board patterns and implementing strategic clicking. Initial attempts involved random clicks, but advanced AI logic improved performance, despite challenges such as shadow banning for high scores. The AI logic combines rules to identify bomb and safe spots efficiently, leading to rapid scores across all game levels.

recent_posts.title: Creating a real guitar controlled Guitar Hero
recent_posts.summary: A developer attempts to create a Guitar Hero game using a real guitar instead of traditional keyboard and mouse inputs. The process involves developing a Python program for note detection, mapping notes to keyboard presses or mouse actions, and adding various features like mouse control, camera movement, and special effects, all while enduring multiple technical challenges.

recent_posts.title: How I recreated Pikmin in a day
recent_posts.summary: The post describes the challenges and experiences of remaking the game Pikmin within a 24-hour timeframe, showcasing the determination and creativity involved in rapid game development.

recent_posts.title: Replicating Poor Quality Mobile Games in Just One Hour: A Challenge
recent_posts.summary: An individual takes on the challenge of recreating low-quality mobile games within an hour using Unity. They attempt to replicate three different mobile games, including one called 'Count Masters', in the limited timeframe, showcasing the ease of recreating simple mobile games.

recent_posts.title: Recreating Poorly Rated Mobile Games in One Hour Using Unity
recent_posts.summary: The challenge was to recreate three badly regarded mobile games within one hour each using Unity. The author goes through the process of setting up basic game mechanics, including movement, obstacles, and scoring. Despite some bugs and limitations due to time constraints, functional versions of games like Count Masters and Attack Hole were developed. The post highlights the difficulties and creative solutions involved in rapid game creation.
